newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALBAK UNBUNDLING ENDS, MOVES JSE SECTOR.
newsitem.headline: MALBAK UNBUNDLING ENDS, MOVES JSE SECTOR.

text.p: Malbak Ltd, the South African conglomerate which last week put the final touches to its unbundling, will move to the packaging and printing sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday, the firm said.

The company, which was previously listed in the industrial holdings sector, now takes on a new guise as a packaging company with its major asssets a 68 percent stake in Kohler Ltd, a 64 percent interest in London-listed MY Holdings and 100 million rand in cash.
Malbak said in a statement that its major assets are valued at around two billion rand.
Its pro forma turnover for the year ended August 31, 1996 was 2.8 billion rand while its operating income amounted to 290 million rand.
On the 337.5 million shares in issue, earnings per share excluding exceptional items, would have been 39.1 cents a share and the dividend on a 2.9 times cover, 13.6 cents a share.

Malbak said that with the restructure of the group, its share price will decrease to reflect the value of its underlying assets. Analysts have estimated that the "new" Malbak should trade at between 750 and 800 cents a share.
Due to certain conditions precedent to the disposal of its stake in Haggie Ltd, Malbak still holds this asset. Shareholders will be informed as soon as resolution is reached.
Malbak also continues to hold its unsold interests in ICL (South Africa) but negotiations are continuing for that disposal.

It said it this week finalised the sale of its interest in engineering business Osborn MMD to Boart Longyear for 10.3 million rand in cash. These funds, plus 32 million rand arising out of dividends paid to Malbak from its unbundled companies will also reside in Malbak.

The group said that analysts in their valuations may not have "appreciated" the net value due to Malbak by the Malbak share trust. The trust holds 5.6 million Malbak shares which currently valued amounts to around 120 million rand.
The trust will receive the shares in the Malbak unbundling which will be disposed of over time, so realising value for shareholders.

Malbak said the the share distribution for Haggie, if applicable, the proceeds and interest on that, also if applicable, from the disposal of Osborn, ICL and Haggie and any other provisions will be available for a possible second distribution.
The group's interim results for the six months ended February 28 will be published towards the end of the first week in May.
Shareholders were reminded that they would receive their distributed shares cum dividend, except for Foodcorp Ltd. Because of this Malbak will not pay an interim dividend.
